clue.text: Rises in opposition concerning horses' dressage movements

parts.note: re means concerning, about
a volt (volte) is a sideways circling step in dressage; plural volts

explanation.surface: A puzzling report about horses rearing up during their dressage routine.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolt is to rise up against authority, so the verb matches rising in opposition.

clue.text: Troubled Ulster's outcomes

indicators.note: troubled says the letters are disturbed into a new order, with a nod to the Troubles in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: The consequences of turmoil in Northern Ireland, known as Ulster.
explanation.definitionFit: Results are the consequences or outcomes of an action or event.

clue.text: Virtuoso, too disrupted, overlooked corrupting influence

indicators.note: disrupted says the letters of too are broken up, scattered through the longer word
overlooked says those letters are left out

explanation.surface: A virtuoso, too troubled, missed a bad influence.
explanation.walkthrough: T, O and O are spread through VIRTUOSO; remove them and the rest spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A virus is figuratively something harmful that spreads and corrupts, as well as a literal pathogen.

clue.text: Comes to shore on promontory for creative sort of gardening

parts.note: lands means comes to shore
a cape is a headland or promontory

explanation.surface: A sailor lands on a headland to do some imaginative gardening.
explanation.definitionFit: Landscape gardening is the art of designing grounds and parks, so the word names that kind.

clue.text: Female record for woolly ruminants

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A woman sets a record for cud-chewing animals with fleeces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep are cud-chewing farm animals with woolly fleeces.

clue.text: Richly furnished residences in buildings around America

indicators.note: around says the word for buildings is wrapped about the letter for America

parts.note: places, in the sense of premises or buildings

explanation.surface: Luxurious homes found in various buildings across America.
explanation.definitionFit: Palaces are grand royal or official homes, typically lavishly decorated and furnished.

clue.text: Melt ore, put mostly in order, for fuel source

indicators.note: in order says the gathered letters are rearranged properly
mostly says the last letter of put is dropped

explanation.surface: Smelting ore and putting things in order to find a source of fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Petroleum is crude oil, from which petrol and other fuels are refined.

clue.text: Unit central to rising infertility

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, says the letters are read upwards, in reverse
central to says the letters come from the middle of infertility

explanation.surface: A measure at the heart of increasing infertility rates.
explanation.definitionFit: A litre is a metric unit of volume, a thousand cubic centimetres.

clue.text: Foolishly locates in land along the shore

indicators.note: foolishly says the letters are arranged in a silly, jumbled way

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly places something in the territory beside the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastline is the outline of land where it meets the sea.

clue.text: Barely sufficient society, principally one advancing cash

indicators.note: principally points to the leading letter of society

parts.note: a lender advances money

explanation.surface: A meagre society, mainly someone lending money.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender means scanty or meagre, as in slender means or a slender majority.

clue.text: Son telephoned during exam — most unusual!

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

indicators.note: during says the calling happens within the exam, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a test is an exam
rang means telephoned

explanation.surface: A boy makes a phone call in the middle of an examination, which is very odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangest is the superlative of strange, meaning the oddest or least usual.

clue.text: Hint of tense competition

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
a race is a competition

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a contest is tense and closely fought.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace is a tiny amount or slight suggestion of something, like a hint of flavour.

clue.text: Fails to win, nearest sides forfeited

indicators.note: the sides of the word for nearest, its outer letters, are given up

parts.note: closest means nearest

explanation.surface: A team fails to win when the nearest sides concede the match.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose is to be defeated, the opposite of winning a contest.

clue.text: Made solemn avowal in favour of trial edition

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: Someone swore solemnly in support of a trial version of a publication.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest can mean to declare or affirm solemnly, as in protesting one's innocence.

clue.text: Advance money to sailor, say, for sandwich

parts.note: a sub is an advance of money, as on wages
a marine is a seagoing soldier, loosely a sailor; 'say' marks the looseness

explanation.surface: Lending a seaman some cash so that he can buy a sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine is a long bread roll filled with meat or cheese, named for its shape.

clue.text: Splendid fish pursued by one worker

indicators.note: pursued by says the fish comes first, with the rest following

parts.note: brill is a flatfish
I is the Roman numeral for one
a worker ant; ant is the crossword worker

explanation.surface: A splendid fish chased by a lone worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant means outstanding, excellent or splendid.

clue.text: Additions in lines on cricket grounds

parts.note: creases are white lines on a cricket pitch marking where batsmen and bowlers stand

explanation.surface: Extra items marked in lines on cricket fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Increases are additions or rises in amount or number.

clue.text: Relatively ironic radical makes a comeback accepting religious instruction

indicators.note: accepting says the turned word takes the instruction letters inside it
makes a comeback says the radical's word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a red is a political radical
RI is the school abbreviation for religious instruction

explanation.surface: An ironic left-winger returns to the fold and takes up religious teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry humour is ironic and understated, so drier is the comparative: more ironic.

clue.text: In trouble, guards the family members

indicators.note: in trouble says these letters are in disarray, reordered

explanation.surface: A parent protects the relatives when they are in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Daughters are female children, members of a family.

clue.text: Apprehend oceans, we're told

indicators.note: we're told says the word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: seas are oceans

explanation.surface: An instruction to arrest the seas, apparently passed on by word of mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize someone is to grab or arrest them, the same as apprehending a suspect.

clue.text: Learned person's panic mostly about short vacation

indicators.note: about says the panic word goes round the short vacation
mostly says the last letter of the word for panic is dropped

parts.note: a scare is a panic

indicators.note: short says the vacation word loses its last letter

parts.note: hols is British slang for holidays, a vacation

explanation.surface: An academic panics a bit over a curtailed holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: SCAR (panic mostly) goes about HOL (short holidays); the 's is just a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a person of great learning, especially in an academic field.

clue.text: Calculators added up people showing promise

indicators.note: up here means in, as in up at university, so the word for added is placed within the promising people

parts.note: comers (up-and-comers) are people likely to succeed
put means added, as in put sugar in tea

explanation.surface: Machines that totted up figures, and the promising people who used them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Added up' reads as one phrase for calculating, but 'added' gives PUT and 'up' puts it inside COMERS, up-and-coming people.
explanation.definitionFit: Computers are machines that calculate; the word once also meant people who did calculations.

clue.text: Rebuked in Telegraph's cold editorial

indicators.note: in says the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone was criticised in a frosty leader column in this newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Scolded means told off or reprimanded, the same as rebuked.

clue.text: Large room, one we organised to show scary movie

parts.note: a hall is a large room

indicators.note: organised says the letters of these two short words are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A group arranged to screen a horror film in a big room.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloween is the 1978 John Carpenter horror film, a classic of the slasher genre.

clue.text: Dispiriting experience, but not at first, for possessor

indicators.note: not at first says the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a downer is a depressing experience

explanation.surface: Ownership is a depressing experience, though not initially.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is the person who possesses something.

clue.text: Pilfers ladies' undergarments, we hear!

indicators.note: we hear says the word is said aloud

parts.note: knicks is short for knickers, British for women's underpants

explanation.surface: Someone steals women's underwear, so the rumour goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Knickers are what the British call women's underpants; nick is British slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick is British slang for to steal, so nicks means pilfers.

clue.text: My weekly greeting

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an exclamation of surprise, like '..., what's this?'
second meaning: ...! is a weekly celebrity magazine
third meaning: the everyday word said when meeting someone

explanation.walkthrough: Three short definitions in a row; 'My weekly' looks like a possessive phrase but each word is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an exclamation of surprise, the title of a weekly magazine and a common salutation.

clue.text: Lake boundary's shelf of rocks

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
an edge is a boundary

explanation.surface: The rim of a lake forms a rocky shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge is a narrow horizontal projection on a cliff or rock face.

clue.text: Knight accompanying King and master

indicators.note: accompanying says the knight's letter goes alongside the king

parts.note: King Lear, Shakespeare's tragic king
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight accompanies the king and his lord.
explanation.definitionFit: To master a skill is to learn it thoroughly; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Accomplished aim, sowed grass round University College court principally

indicators.note: round says the word for sowed grass goes about the other letters

parts.note: seeded means sowed grass seed

indicators.note: principally points to the leading letter of court

explanation.surface: A groundsman achieved his goal by seeding the lawn around the college court.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed is to achieve what was intended, so it is a synonym of accomplishing an aim.

clue.text: Retiring maestro tersely frames sharp responses

indicators.note: Retiring says the hidden letters are read backwards
frames says the two words enclose the answer's letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A shy conductor who speaks curtly comes up with quick put-downs.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'frames' into the definition, but it is the signal that maestro tersely holds the letters, leaving 'sharp responses' as the plural definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a quick, witty or cutting reply to a remark.

clue.text: Delay for a time America blocking outlay

indicators.note: blocking says the letters for America stand in the middle of the outlay, obstructing it

parts.note: spend is a noun meaning outlay, amount spent

explanation.surface: America obstructs spending, causing a temporary hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to postpone it or halt it temporarily.
